response.rationale: C1 is the most complete fixed candidate: it retains the diagnosis of CMV colitis by being compatible with the CMV immunostain-positive viral cytopathic inclusions, and it adds rectal localization from imaging and endoscopic ulcers. R2 has the definitive virologic raw span but omits the rectal anatomy. R3 is contradicted by the viral inclusions despite overlapping colitis/crypt distortion, and R4 has no ischemic-specific raw support and lacks typical pain features.

rejected.why: Cardiac history and hematochezia are nonspecific; no raw span supports ischemic colitis, and the viral inclusions and rectal ulcer morphology favor CMV.
Active colitis, crypt distortion, and reactive changes overlap, but the raw viral cytopathic inclusions with CMV immunostain directly disconfirm idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease.
